method.label: Count one solution per floor interval

annotationRationale: Floor intervals turn the equation into intersections with constant levels. A factored difference proves monotonicity and uniqueness, continuity supplies existence, and an integer inequality counts the eligible intervals.
sourceMethod: Follows the official parabola and horizontal-step intersection method. Uses the official fractional-part bound first, then supplies a monotonicity proof and explicit endpoint reasoning to justify the intersection count.

review.mathCheck: The fractional-part bound forces \(-100<x<100\). On each floor interval, the factored difference proves that \(P(x)=10000x-x^2\) is strictly increasing. Continuity and the excluded right endpoint give exactly one solution precisely when \((k+1)^2<10000\). Thus \(k=-100,\ldots,98\) contributes 199 solutions, choice C. The root at zero is included; the potential endpoint at 100 is excluded.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of the second MAA Q24 approach on pages 16-17, preceded by the official fractional-part bound. It replaces reliance on graphical intersection intuition with explicit monotonicity and continuity arguments.
review.annotationCheck: Negative floor intervals, existence, uniqueness and half-open endpoints are handled correctly. The explanation is self-contained without the official graph.
